name_en: Namerou — pounded raw fish with miso from the Boso coast
summary_ja: 揺れる船の上で獲れたてのアジをさばき、味噌とねぎ、しょうがとともに粘りが出るまで叩いた漁師料理。醤油だとこぼれるため味噌を使ったといい、皿までなめたくなる旨さが名の由来と伝わる。
summary_en: Fresh-caught horse mackerel is pounded with miso, scallion, and ginger right on a rocking boat until it turns sticky — miso was used instead of soy sauce because soy sauce spilled on deck, and the name is said to come from wanting to lick the plate clean.
source_title: なめろう 千葉県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Kaisou — jellied seaweed for New Year's, made from kotoji-tsunomata
summary_ja: 岩場に生えるコトジツノマタという海藻を煮溶かし、型に流して固めた寒天状の一品。年末に銚子の商人が正月用に売り歩いたことからお節に加わり、味の濃いお節の箸休めとして食べられてきたという。
summary_en: A seaweed called kotoji-tsunomata is simmered until it thickens, then set in a mold like a firm jelly — merchants from Choshi are said to have sold it door to door each year-end, and it became a palate-cleanser among the heavier dishes of osechi.
source_title: かいそう 千葉県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

summary_ja: 掘りたての生の落花生をさやごと塩水でゆでる、千葉の産地ならではの季節の味。生の落花生は収穫後すぐに硬くなり出すため、掘りたてをすぐゆでないとおいしくならないという。
summary_en: Freshly dug peanuts, still in their shells, are boiled whole in salted water — a taste unique to the growing region, since raw peanuts start hardening the moment they're pulled from the ground and need to be boiled almost immediately.
source_title: ゆで落花生 千葉県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Rakkasei Miso — peanuts stirred into sweet miso
summary_ja: 市場に出回らない規格外の落花生を、味噌や砂糖と合わせて炒りつける常備菜。今ほど食料が豊かでなかった時代、農家が余った落花生を無駄にしない工夫から生まれたと伝わる。
summary_en: Peanuts too small or misshapen to sell are stirred into miso and sugar and toasted into a pantry relish — said to have started as a way for farm households to use up peanuts the market wouldn't take, in leaner years.
source_title: 落花生味噌 千葉県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Chikko Toufu — curd made from cow's first milk
summary_ja: 出産直後の牛から搾れる初乳を温め、酢を加えて分離させた素朴な豆腐状の一品。8代将軍徳川吉宗が嶺岡牧で白牛を飼育させたことが日本の酪農の始まりとされ、酪農家の間で食べ継がれてきたという。
summary_en: A cow's first milk after calving is warmed and split with a little vinegar into a plain curd — tied to the story of shogun Tokugawa Yoshimune's white cattle raised at the Mineoka pastures, said to be the start of dairy farming in Japan, and long eaten among the region's dairy households.
source_title: チッコ豆腐／牛乳豆腐 千葉県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

name_en: Sumitsukare — grated daikon simmered with soybeans and sake lees, a Chiba version
summary_ja: 鬼おろしで粗くおろした大根と人参を、節分の豆や酒かすと一緒に煮た料理。栃木県から伝わったとされ、2月最初の午の日にお稲荷様へ供えてから食べる。茨城や埼玉にも同じ名の郷土料理が伝わっている。
summary_en: Daikon and carrot, coarsely grated with a rough-toothed oni-oroshi grater, are simmered with leftover setsubun soybeans and sake lees — said to have traveled from Tochigi into Chiba's Higashikatsushika area, offered to the local inari shrine on the year's first Day of the Horse before being eaten. Ibaraki and Saitama carry dishes of the same name.
source_title: すみつかれ 千葉県 | うちの郷土料理：農林水産省
